# Use lean-canvas

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Turn a startup or internal-product idea into a lean canvas that finds what could kill it — the nine boxes filled only from what the user said, each entry tagged evidence-backed (with its source) or assumption, the assumptions ranked by how likely each is wrong times how badly the idea fails if it is, the cheapest test with a pass/fail line set in advance for the top ones, a computed unit-economics check when price and costs are given, and a plain call when the idea should change before anything is built.

**Reach for it when** the user says "lean canvas", "help me think through my startup idea", "what are the riskiest assumptions", "how do I validate this idea", "is this idea worth building", or "poke holes in my business model".

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install lean-canvas                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install lean-canvas --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install lean-canvas --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Product manager pack: [`--pack product-manager`](../packs/use-the-product-manager-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

It ships scripts, so it needs Python 3 (standard library only, nothing to install). What they may touch is declared in [its manifest](../../../packs/product-manager/skills/lean-canvas/manifest.json).

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Fill in a lean canvas for my idea: a subscription app that plans weekly meals for parents of kids with food allergies"
- "What are the riskiest assumptions in my startup idea, and how do I test them before I write any code?"
- "Poke holes in my business model — $49/month, we pay about $300 to get each customer, they stay around five months"
- "I want to pitch an internal tool to the ops leadership team. Is it worth building, and what should I validate first?"
- "How do I validate this idea cheaply this month? It's a marketplace for renting camping gear between neighbours"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Write the business case for the new routing platform with build, buy and do-nothing options and NPV for the steering committee"
- "The exec team approved the idea — write the press release and FAQ working backwards from launch"
- "Run a Five Forces analysis on the meal-kit market before we decide whether to enter"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use lean-canvas".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **The first lines are the riskiest assumption and its test**, not the canvas.
- **Every canvas entry carries a tag**, and every `[evidence]` names the source the user gave.
- **Wrong-segment and opinion-only evidence is downgraded** and said to be.
- **A feature claimed as an unfair advantage is moved out**, and the box reads "none yet" if nothing else qualifies.
- **Each channel is checked against the early adopter**, mismatches named.
- **Unit economics are computed with the derivation shown**, and payback longer than lifetime is flagged.
- **Each top test has a sample, a pre-set pass/fail line, a cost and a time.**
- **Nothing is invented**: no market sizes, competitors, prices, churn or channels the user didn't give.

## Use something else when

- An investment case with options, NPV, payback ranges and a sponsor — `business-case`
- The press release and FAQ for an idea that is already approved — `prfaq`
- Market attractiveness, competitors, SWOT or Five Forces — `strategy-analysis`
- How to measure a feature that has shipped or is about to — `success-metrics`
- Turning interview notes or tickets already collected into themes — `feedback-synthesis`
